name: Idaho
headline_status: Cannabis is fully illegal in Idaho for both recreational and medical use.
summary: Idaho has no medical or adult-use cannabis program, and possessing even small amounts is a criminal misdemeanor; since January 1, 2026 that offense carries a mandatory minimum $300 fine. Hemp products may not contain any THC. On November 3, 2026, voters rejected HJR 4, a constitutional amendment that would have barred citizen initiatives on cannabis, by roughly two to one, so the initiative route to legalization stays open.

possession_limit.value: No amount is legal. Possession of 3 ounces or less is a misdemeanor; more than 3 ounces is a felony.

penalties.value: 3 oz or less: misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and up to $1,000, with a mandatory minimum $300 fine under H0007 (effective January 1, 2026). Over 3 oz up to 1 lb: felony, up to 5 years and $10,000.

home_grow.value: Not allowed. Growing any amount is a felony, with mandatory minimum prison terms starting at 25 plants or 1 pound.

retail_sales.value: None. Idaho licenses no cannabis businesses of any kind.

medical_program.value: None. A 2026 medical cannabis initiative fell short of the ballot with 58,024 verified signatures against 70,725 required.

hemp_thc.value: Idaho was the last state to legalize hemp production and allows no THC at all in hemp products.

purchase_age.value: No legal purchase of marijuana for any age; there are no licensed adult-use or medical marijuana sales.

public_use.value: Not allowed anywhere: there is no legal recreational or medical marijuana use, so using it in public or private can lead to possession charges.

tourists.value: No. There are no legal marijuana sales, out-of-state medical cards are not recognized, and visitors face the same possession penalties as residents.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Idaho has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DUI requires evidence of impairment.

timeline.event: Legislature refers HJR 4, an amendment to bar citizen-initiated drug legalization, to the 2026 ballot
H0007 takes effect, imposing a mandatory minimum $300 fine for simple possession
Medical cannabis initiative fails to qualify for the November ballot
Voters defeat HJR 4, about 66% No to 34% Yes (unofficial)

faq.a: No. Idaho bans both recreational and medical cannabis, and possessing any amount is a crime.

faq.q: What is the penalty for marijuana possession in Idaho?
faq.a: Up to 3 ounces is a misdemeanor punishable by up to a year in jail and a $1,000 fine, with a $300 minimum fine since 2026. More than 3 ounces is a felony.
Only hemp products with no THC at all are allowed under Idaho law.

faq.q: What happened with Idaho's marijuana amendment in 2026?
faq.a: Voters rejected HJR 4 on November 3, 2026, by roughly 66% to 34%, so citizens keep the ability to propose cannabis initiatives.
